answer: An applicant enters the ledger only after locking a measured saffron deposit and filing one signed sonnet whose closing couplet hashes its address to the epoch seed. Each later request leaves a plume of timestamps, counterparties, and wording. Settlement admits the identity only when that plume stays statistically apart from existing agents and the sonnet is lexically distant from prior filings. A shared saffron vault, a recycled couplet, or a plume that braids into an existing cluster slashes the deposit and voids the seat, so cheap clones destroy collateral instead of multiplying votes.
